eventSubject: FDA 2023 COVID-19 vaccine formula selection and manufacturer authorization
curationMethod: Independent dated FDA press releases verified by public FDA pages; curator paraphrases not publication-time snapshots

claims.text: FDA amended the emergency use authorizations of the Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech bivalent mRNA COVID-19 vaccines to simplify dose schedules for most people.
FDA said an advisory committee would discuss fall 2023 strain composition in June before decisions on updated vaccines and future formulations.
FDA advised manufacturers developing updated 2023-2024 COVID-19 vaccines to use a monovalent XBB.1.5 composition, incorporating advisory committee input.
FDA anticipated manufacturers submitting supporting data and filings for future agency action on updated vaccines before fall availability.
FDA approved and authorized updated 2023-2024 mRNA COVID-19 vaccines for ModernaTX and Pfizer with a monovalent Omicron XBB.1.5 component.
FDA said earlier bivalent Moderna and Pfizer-BioNTech vaccines were no longer authorized in the United States after the updated formula action.
FDA amended the Novavax adjuvanted COVID-19 vaccine emergency use authorization for the 2023-2024 monovalent XBB.1.5 formula for people 12 years and older.
FDA presented the updated Novavax protein-based vaccine authorization as another option following the separate ModernaTX and Pfizer mRNA authorizations.

curatedEdges.basis: April's announcement left fall strain formulation to future advisory discussions, while FDA's June update subsequently recommended a specific XBB.1.5 composition.
June's manufacturer formula guidance anticipated data submissions and agency decisions, and September FDA announcements authorized specific updated mRNA products.
September FDA approvals and authorizations covered mRNA vaccines made by ModernaTX and Pfizer, whereas October's further authorization covered the distinct Novavax adjuvanted product.
